### Investments

Clinton has advocated for affordability and improved quality pediatric services for parents.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-72) In 2022, she invested in Summer Health, a startup pediatric [telehealth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telehealth "Telehealth") platform that offers virtual care services connecting parents with pediatricians, sleep coaches, and lactation experts.[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-73)

### Author

#### Children's non-fiction

In September 2015, Clinton's first children's book, _It's Your World: Get Informed, Get Inspired and Get Going!_, was published by [Philomel Books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philomel_Books "Philomel Books"). The 400-page book is aimed at middle school students (ages 10 to 14) and introduces them to a range of social issues, encouraging them to take action to make the world a better place.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-NYT-Rvw-74)[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-75)[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-76) The paperback edition was published by [Puffin Books](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puffin_Books "Puffin Books") in 2017.[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-apyourworld-77)[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-touryourworldcnn-78)

In May 2017, her second children's book, _She Persisted: 13 American Women Who Changed the World_, illustrated by Alexandra Boiger, was published by Philomel Books. Upon its release, the book became a bestseller,[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-79) reaching No.1 on _The New York Times_ Children's Picture Books Best Sellers list on July 30, 2017.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-nytbestpersisted-80) In 2019, she worked with the Berkeley, California's Bay Area Children's Theater in adapting the book into a musical play, _She Persisted: The Musical_,[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-81) which ran from January to March.[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-82)[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-83)

In 2018, Clinton wrote a companion book featuring women around the world entitled _She Persisted Around the World: 13 Women Who Changed History_.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-84) The book debuted at No.2 on the _Times'_ Children's Picture Books Best Sellers list.[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-85)

Clinton's fourth children's book, _Start Now!: You Can Make a Difference_, was published by Philomel in 2018. It is aimed at empowering young would-be activists aged seven to ten, addressing themes ranging from bullying to climate change to endangered species.[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-peoplestart-87) In interviews, she talked about how she drew on her personal experiences and strategies for dealing with bullies growing up and as an adult.[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-apbully-88)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-peoplestart-87)

In 2019, Clinton published her fifth children's book, _Don't Let Them Disappear: 12 Endangered Species Across the Globe_. The book, illustrated by Gianna Marino, is about endangered animals and is aimed at teaching children aged four to eight about species in need of protection.[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-89)[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-90)[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-91)

Clinton continued her children's "She Persisted" series in 2020 with _She Persisted in Sports: American Olympians Who Changed the Game_, also published by Philomel. Again illustrated by Alexandra Boiger, this chapter book celebrates women in sports who broke records and smashed barriers with their persistence.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-92)

#### Co-authored with Hillary Clinton

In 2019, Clinton co-wrote a book with her mother, [Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton"), titled _[The Book of Gutsy Women: Favorite Stories of Courage and Resilience](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Book\_of\_Gutsy\_Women:\_Favorite\_Stories\_of\_Courage\_and\_Resilience "The Book of Gutsy Women: Favorite Stories of Courage and Resilience")_ and they embarked on a multi-city book tour together.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-93)

In 2020, the mother-daughter writing duo published _Grandma's Gardens_, a children's book. The book was inspired by Hillary's mother, [Dorothy Rodham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorothy_Rodham "Dorothy Rodham"), who had a passion for gardening.[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-gg-94)

#### Scholarly work

Clinton co-authored a highly praised scholarly work on global health policy with Devi Sridhar, entitled _Governing Global Health: Who Runs the World and Why?_, published in 2017 by [Oxford University Press](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford_University_Press "Oxford University Press"). The book examines the role of partnerships between public and private entities in addressing global health issues.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-95)[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-96)

### Speaking engagements

In February 2024, Clinton hosted a panel at Harvard Graduate School of Education on the topic of climate change and education, focusing on the role of educators in improving the lives of children affected by climate change.[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-97)

## Political activities

### Hillary Clinton 2008 presidential campaign

Main article: [Hillary Clinton 2008 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton_2008_presidential_campaign "Hillary Clinton 2008 presidential campaign")

[![Image 10](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/c9/Chelsea_Clinton_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-Chelsea_Clinton_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chelsea_Clinton_(cropped).jpg)

Clinton campaigning for her mother in March 2008

In December 2007, Clinton began campaigning in Iowa in support of her mother's bid for the Democratic presidential nomination.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-Iowa_join-98) She appeared across the country, largely on college campuses.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-99)[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-100)[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-101) By early April 2008, she had spoken at 100 colleges on behalf of her mother's candidacy.[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-chelseavoice-102)

While campaigning, Clinton answered audience questions but did not give interviews or respond to press questions,[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-reuters_32508-103) including one from a nine-year-old _[Scholastic News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scholastic\_News\_Kids\_Press\_Corps "Scholastic News Kids Press Corps")_ reporter asking whether her father would be a good "first man".[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-topdog-104) She replied, "I'm sorry, I don't talk to the press and that applies to you, unfortunately. Even though I think you're cute."[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-scholastic-105)[Philippe Reines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippe_Reines "Philippe Reines"), her mother's [press secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_secretary "Press secretary"), intervened when the press attempted to approach Chelsea directly.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-topdog-104)

When [MSNBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MSNBC "MSNBC") reporter [David Shuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Shuster "David Shuster") characterized Clinton's participation in her mother's campaign as "sort of being pimped out", the Clinton campaign objected. Shuster subsequently apologized on-air and was suspended for two weeks.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-shusterwp-106)[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-107)

The first time she was asked about her mother's handling of the [Clinton–Lewinsky scandal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton%E2%80%93Lewinsky_scandal "Clinton–Lewinsky scandal") at a campaign stop Clinton responded, "I do not think that is any of your business."[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-chelseavoice-102) As she became a more experienced campaigner, she refined her responses and deflected questions on the issue with comments such as, "If that's what you want to vote on, that's what you should vote on. But I think there are other people [who are] going to vote on things like healthcare and economics."[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-chelseavoice-102)[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-AP_impeach-108)

Hillary Clinton conceded the 2008 Democratic presidential nomination to [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") on June 7, 2008.[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-109) At the [2008 Democratic National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Democratic_National_Convention "2008 Democratic National Convention"), Chelsea called Hillary "my hero and my mother" and introduced her with a long video tribute.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-wsj-110)

### Hillary Clinton 2016 presidential campaign

Main article: [Hillary Clinton 2016 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton_2016_presidential_campaign "Hillary Clinton 2016 presidential campaign")

[![Image 11](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/86/Chelsea_Clinton_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg/250px-Chelsea_Clinton_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Chelsea_Clinton_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)

Clinton speaks at a 2016 campaign rally for her mother.

As she did in 2008, Clinton again took an active part in her mother's presidential campaign in 2016,[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-nyt011216-111) expanding her role as surrogate at more than 200 public events across the country, including and beyond college campuses.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-cnn_72816-112) In July 2016, she introduced her mother at the [Democratic National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2016_Democratic_National_Convention "2016 Democratic National Convention") in Philadelphia,[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-2016DNC-113) in a personal, emotional tribute[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-cnn_72816-112) recalling her own upbringing and describing her mother's commitment to issues and to public service.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-2016DNCtranscript-114)

Even before her mother received the Democratic nomination, Clinton frequently spoke out against candidate [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump")'s positions and rhetoric.[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-cnn_72816-112) At one appearance in September 2016, while answering a question about her mother's position supporting [medical marijuana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_cannabis_in_the_United_States "Medical cannabis in the United States") research, Clinton got some attention for an inaccurate comment she made regarding drug interactions with marijuana; she walked back the comment a few days later, acknowledging that she misspoke.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-washpo_092816-115)

On November 9, 2016, Hillary Clinton conceded the presidential race to Republican candidate [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump").[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-116) After the 2016 election, Chelsea Clinton's political commentary on her [Twitter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") account led to speculation that she might have political aspirations of her own.[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-wp_politics-117)

## Personal life

Clinton married investment banker [Marc Mezvinsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marc_Mezvinsky "Marc Mezvinsky")[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-engaged-118) on July 31, 2010, in an [interfaith ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interfaith_marriage "Interfaith marriage") at the Astor Courts estate[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-119) in [Rhinebeck, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhinebeck,_New_York "Rhinebeck, New York"). Mezvinsky is Jewish,[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-NYT_wedding-120) and his parents, [Marjorie Margolies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marjorie_Margolies "Marjorie Margolies") and [Edward Mezvinsky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edward_Mezvinsky "Edward Mezvinsky"), are both former members of Congress. The senior Clintons and Mezvinskys were friends in the 1990s and their children met on a [Renaissance Weekend](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_Weekend "Renaissance Weekend") retreat in [Hilton Head Island, South Carolina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilton_Head_Island,_South_Carolina "Hilton Head Island, South Carolina").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-121) They first were reported to be a couple in 2005, and they became engaged over [Thanksgiving](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thanksgiving "Thanksgiving") weekend in 2009.[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-engaged-118)

Following their wedding, the couple lived in New York City's [Gramercy Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gramercy_Park "Gramercy Park") neighborhood for three years[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-NYT_wedding-120) and later purchased a $10.5 million condominium in the [NoMad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NoMad,_Manhattan "NoMad, Manhattan") district of Manhattan.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-IBT31513-122) Their first child, a daughter named Charlotte, was born on September 26, 2014.[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-NYT-birth-123) Their second child, a son named Aidan, was born on June 18, 2016.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-124)[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-125) Shortly after Aidan was born, the family moved to the nearby [Flatiron District](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flatiron_District "Flatiron District").[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-126) Their third child, a son named Jasper, was born on July 22, 2019.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelsea_Clinton#cite_note-127)

_**Derry Girls**_ is a [period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_drama "Historical drama")[teen sitcom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_sitcom "Teen sitcom") set in [Derry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry "Derry"), Northern Ireland, created and written by [Lisa McGee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_McGee "Lisa McGee"), that premiered on 4 January 2018 on UK-based broadcaster [Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_4 "Channel 4")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-BARB-4) and ran for three series. The channel's most successful comedy since _[Father Ted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Father\_Ted "Father Ted")_, the series was inspired by McGee's own experiences growing up in an Irish Catholic family in [Derry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry "Derry"), [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland"), in the 1990s, during the final years of [the Troubles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Troubles "The Troubles").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-5) It stars [Saoirse-Monica Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saoirse-Monica_Jackson "Saoirse-Monica Jackson"), [Louisa Harland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisa_Harland "Louisa Harland"), [Nicola Coughlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Coughlan "Nicola Coughlan"), [Jamie-Lee O'Donnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie-Lee_O'Donnell "Jamie-Lee O'Donnell"), and [Dylan Llewellyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_Llewellyn "Dylan Llewellyn") as five teenagers living in mid-1990s Derry while attending Our Lady Immaculate College, a fictional [girls' Catholic secondary school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_school "Catholic school") based on the real-life [Thornhill College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thornhill_College "Thornhill College"), where McGee herself studied.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-7) Produced by British production company [Hat Trick Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hat_Trick_Productions "Hat Trick Productions"), _Derry Girls_ was filmed in Northern Ireland, with most scenes shot on location in Derry and some in [Belfast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belfast "Belfast").

Although the plot lines of _Derry Girls_ are fictional, the series frequently references actual events of the Troubles and the [Northern Ireland peace process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland_peace_process "Northern Ireland peace process"), including the 1994 IRA ceasefire announcement, the 1995 visit to Northern Ireland of President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") and First Lady [Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton"), and the [Good Friday referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Friday_Agreement "Good Friday Agreement") of 1998. Archival footage relating to key political figures such as [Ian Paisley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Paisley "Ian Paisley"), [Gerry Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerry_Adams "Gerry Adams"), [Martin McGuinness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_McGuinness "Martin McGuinness"), [John Hume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hume "John Hume") and [Mo Mowlam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mo_Mowlam "Mo Mowlam") is shown via TV and radio broadcasts in family homes. The soundtrack features popular music of the era, by acts including [The Undertones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Undertones "The Undertones"), [Ace of Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ace_of_Base "Ace of Base"), [Blur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blur_(band) "Blur (band)"), [Cypress Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cypress_Hill "Cypress Hill"), [Salt-N-Pepa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt-N-Pepa "Salt-N-Pepa"), [Enya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enya "Enya"), [the Corrs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Corrs "The Corrs"), [Boyzone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boyzone "Boyzone"), [Scarlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarlet_(British_band) "Scarlet (British band)"), [Fatboy Slim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatboy_Slim "Fatboy Slim"), [PJ & Duncan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant_&_Dec_discography "Ant & Dec discography"), and [the Cranberries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cranberries "The Cranberries").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-8)

The first series, broadcast on Channel 4 in January and February 2018,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-9) became the most-watched series in Northern Ireland since modern records began in 2002. The series was renewed shortly after the pilot episode aired, and the second series was broadcast in March and April 2019. A third and final series set in 1996[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-10) and 1997[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-Special-11) was commissioned for 2020, although filming was delayed due to the [COVID-19 pandemic's impact on television production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_on_television "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on television"),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-13) and premiered in April 2022.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-DG3-15) A final special extended 45-minute episode titled "The Agreement", set in 1998 during the signing of the [Good Friday Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Friday_Agreement "Good Friday Agreement"), aired on 18 May 2022.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-Special-11)

_Derry Girls_ has inspired a mural of its main characters painted on the side of Badgers Bar and Restaurant at 18 Orchard Street, Derry, which has become a popular tourist attraction.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-16)

## Synopsis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Synopsis")]

The series follows Erin Quinn ([Saoirse-Monica Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saoirse-Monica_Jackson "Saoirse-Monica Jackson")), her cousin Orla ([Louisa Harland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisa_Harland "Louisa Harland")), their friends Clare ([Nicola Coughlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Coughlan "Nicola Coughlan")), Michelle ([Jamie-Lee O'Donnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie-Lee_O'Donnell "Jamie-Lee O'Donnell")), and Michelle's English cousin James ([Dylan Llewellyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_Llewellyn "Dylan Llewellyn")) as they navigate their teenage years during the end of [the Troubles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Troubles "The Troubles") in [Derry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry "Derry"), where they all attend a [Catholic girls' secondary school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_school "Catholic school"). The friends frequently find themselves in absurd situations amid the political unrest and cultural divides of the times.

## Cast and characters

### Main

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Main")]

*   [Saoirse-Monica Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saoirse-Monica_Jackson "Saoirse-Monica Jackson") as Erin Quinn. Aged 16 at the start of the series, she is passionate and ambitious, with literary aspirations, but is at times vain, self-centred, or overly concerned with how she is regarded by others.
*   [Louisa Harland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisa_Harland "Louisa Harland") as Orla McCool. Aged 15 at the start of the series, she is Erin's detached and eccentric maternal cousin, addicted to sweets. She takes many things literally, misses social cues, and generally is happy to live in her own world.
*   [Nicola Coughlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Coughlan "Nicola Coughlan") as Clare Devlin. Intelligent and studious, often the Girls' voice of reason, she is more intimidated than her friends by authority figures. At the end of series one, she [comes out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming_out "Coming out") as a lesbian.
*   [Jamie-Lee O'Donnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie-Lee_O'Donnell "Jamie-Lee O'Donnell") as Michelle Mallon. The "wild" one of the group, she often gets her friends into trouble through her keen interest in sex, drugs, and alcohol.
*   [Dylan Llewellyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_Llewellyn "Dylan Llewellyn") as James Maguire. Michelle's maternal cousin, who has grown up in London but his mother brings him to live in Derry just before the start of the series; she moves back to London without telling him at the end of the first episode. Out of concern for his safety at the local Christian Brothers school, James becomes the first male pupil at Our Lady Immaculate College. Although the girls make fun of James, they care about him and eventually accept him as a Derry Girl. Everyone believes he is gay, despite his protestations.
*   [Tara Lynne O'Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tara_Lynne_O'Neill "Tara Lynne O'Neill") as Mary Quinn. Erin and Anna's mother and the matriarch of the Quinn family, she has been married to Gerry for 17 years at the start of the series.
*   [Tommy Tiernan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Tiernan "Tommy Tiernan") as Gerry Quinn. Mary's husband and Erin and Anna's father, he is from [Navan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navan "Navan") and works as a delivery driver. He has a strained relationship with his father-in-law, and patiently tries to be the voice of reason despite almost constant mockery and dismissal from those around him.
*   [Kathy Kiera Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathy_Kiera_Clarke "Kathy Kiera Clarke") as Sarah McCool. Orla's mother, Erin and Anna's maternal aunt and Mary's younger sister, she is sweet but dim-witted, heavily focused on her own and other people's appearances. She is an inattentive mother and takes little responsibility for raising Orla, but is still very affectionate towards her.
*   [Ian McElhinney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_McElhinney "Ian McElhinney") as Joe McCool. Mary and Sarah's father, and Erin, Anna and Orla's grandfather, he moved in with the Quinns after his wife died ten years before the start of the series. Joe shows nothing but contempt for Gerry, constantly criticising him and encouraging Mary to leave him, and is fiercely protective of his daughters and granddaughters.
*   [Siobhán McSweeney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siobh%C3%A1n_McSweeney "Siobhán McSweeney") as Sister George Michael, a [Catholic nun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_nun "Catholic nun"). The headmistress of Our Lady Immaculate College, she rules the school with an iron fist. Acid-tongued and unflappable, she views being a nun as a job rather than a calling, treating priests with indifference or even contempt.
*   [Leah O'Rourke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leah_O'Rourke "Leah O'Rourke") as Jenny Joyce, a [prefect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_prefect "School prefect") and sycophant despised by the Girls. She is from a wealthy family and lives in a large house with eight bedrooms, in which she often hosts lavish parties. Her mother Janette used to be friends with Mary, Sarah, Geraldine (Clare's mum) and Deirdre (Michelle's mum) when they were teenagers but since distanced herself after marrying a surgeon.

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Production")]

Filming took place in [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland"), with most scenes shot in [Derry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry "Derry") and [Belfast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belfast "Belfast").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-21) The scenes onboard the train in S3 E3 took place at the [Downpatrick and County Down Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downpatrick_and_County_Down_Railway "Downpatrick and County Down Railway") in [Downpatrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downpatrick "Downpatrick"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-22) with the end of the episode shot at the then-recently-closed [Barry's Amusements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry's_Amusements "Barry's Amusements") in [Portrush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portrush "Portrush").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-23) The first series was filmed from May to July 2017 and released in January and February 2018.

The show was renewed for a second series shortly after the airing of the pilot episode of the first series. Production of the second series began on 8 October 2018.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-25) The second series began airing on 5 March 2019.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-S2-17) On 9 April 2019, immediately after the second series finale, it was confirmed by Channel 4 that _Derry Girls_ would return for a third series.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-27) Production of the third series was due to commence in the spring of 2020, but was suspended following the announcement of the [COVID-19 lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_lockdowns "COVID-19 lockdowns").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-28) On 21 July 2021, Nicola Coughlan confirmed that filming for the third series was set to commence in late 2021, with a premiere in early 2022.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-29) On 23 September 2021, series creator and writer Lisa McGee confirmed Derry Girls would end with its third series, stating "it was always the plan to say goodbye after three series."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-30) On 21 December 2021, McGee and Coughlan announced on social media that filming of the final series had completed.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-radiotimes-31)

## Broadcast

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Broadcast")]

The first series premiered on Channel 4 in the United Kingdom on Thursday nights at 10:00 pm, while the second series was moved to Tuesday nights at 9:15 pm, with the exception of the sixth episode, which was aired at 9:00 pm. The entire series is available to stream in the UK on [All 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_4 "All 4").

The series was picked up by [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") internationally, with series 1 being released on 21 December 2018.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-32) Series 2 was released on 2 August 2019.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-33) The international version of the first series is now available to stream on Netflix in the UK and Ireland. The second series was added on 9 July 2020; however, it was temporarily removed from the service, as it was mistakenly released a year early.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-34) The third and final series was released on 7 October 2022.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-35)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Reception")]

_Derry Girls_ became Channel 4's most successful comedy since _[Father Ted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Father\_Ted "Father Ted")_.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-McClements-37) On [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the first series holds an approval rating of 100% based on reviews from 24 critics with an average rating of 7.9/10. The website's critics consensus states: "A perfectly curated cast and raw writing drive _Derry Girls_'s dark humor as creator Lisa McGee makes frenetic light of teen life in 1990s Northern Ireland".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-38)

The second series has an approval rating of 97%, based on reviews from 33 critics with an average rating of 8.3/10. The website's critics consensus states: "The sophomore season of _Derry Girls_ doesn't lose any of its irreverent charms thanks to its predictably unpredictable romps and canny characterizations".[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-39)

The third series holds an approval rating of 100%, based on reviews from 21 critics with an average rating of 8.9/10. The website's critics consensus states: "Parting is such sweet sorrow, but _Derry Girls_' final season promises to milk as many laughs as it can before viewers say a fond farewell to this lovable band of miscreants."[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-40) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a weighted average, it received a score of 86 out of 100 based on five critic reviews.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-41)

_Derry Girls_ was the most watched series in Northern Ireland since modern records began in 2002, with an average audience of 519,000 and a 64.2 per cent share of the audience.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-42)[Una Mullally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Una_Mullally "Una Mullally") of _[The Irish Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Irish\_Times "The Irish Times")_ praised the series: "The writing in _Derry Girls_ is sublime, the performances perfect, the casting is brilliant."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-43) On 11 January 2018, after the first episode had aired, the programme was renewed for a second series.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-ratings-44) Each episode was watched by over two million people.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-BARB-4) At the conclusion of the first series, Barbara Ellen of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ wrote that _Derry Girls_ evoked such programmes as _[The Inbetweeners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Inbetweeners "The Inbetweeners")_, _[Father Ted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Father\_Ted "Father Ted")_ and _[Bad Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad\_Education\_(TV\_series) "Bad Education (TV series)")_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-45)

### Public reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Public reception")]

As there are slight political undertones to the show, responses have highlighted the comedic nature as keeping the material lighthearted enough to enjoy. Certain writers from various online articles have noted that their own Northern Irish family appreciated the way the show gave an honest portrayal of how life was for teens in the Troubles, and how much was endured by families during that time.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-N._Jones_2019-46) The way it portrayed the events and circumstances with a sense of normality echoed the real lives of both Protestants and Catholics in that area.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-N._Jones_2019-46)

Lisa McGee based events in the programme on her own life, such as writing a letter to the [Clintons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_family "Clinton family")' daughter, Chelsea.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-47) Adding real stories such as this to the episodes grounded the show in a way that allowed viewers to connect with the teenage attitudes of the characters, and served as a stark contrast to the events around them. The juxtaposition of the Troubles violence and teenage life resonated with many viewers.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-48) At 18 Orchard Street in Derry,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-49) a mural of the main cast of characters can be seen on the side of Badger's Bar.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-McClements-37)

## Merchandise

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=17 "Edit section: Merchandise")]

A _Derry Girls_ book, titled _Erin's Diary: An Official Derry Girls Book_, was released on 12 November 2020 by Trapeze Books.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-68) In April 2022, a relaunch of the now-defunct British magazine _[Smash Hits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smash\_Hits "Smash Hits")_, which ceased publication in 2006, issued a special, one-off edition, featuring _Derry Girls_, in promotion for its third series.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-69)

## In other media

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: In other media")]

### _The Crystal Maze_ special

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=19 "Edit section: The Crystal Maze special")]

Cast members [Saoirse-Monica Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saoirse-Monica_Jackson "Saoirse-Monica Jackson"), [Jamie-Lee O'Donnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie-Lee_O'Donnell "Jamie-Lee O'Donnell"), [Louisa Harland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisa_Harland "Louisa Harland"), [Nicola Coughlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Coughlan "Nicola Coughlan") and [Dylan Llewellyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_Llewellyn "Dylan Llewellyn") appeared in a 2018 special episode of the British [game show](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_show "Game show")_[The Crystal Maze](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Crystal\_Maze "The Crystal Maze")_.[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-70) The episode raised money for [Stand Up to Cancer UK](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stand_Up_to_Cancer_(UK) "Stand Up to Cancer (UK)") and was well received by viewers and fans of the show.[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-71)

### _Great British Bake Off_ New Year's episode

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Great British Bake Off New Year's episode")]

For the 2020 New Year holiday, the cast competed on a special episode of _[The Great British Bake Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Great\_British\_Bake\_Off "The Great British Bake Off")_. Cast members Coughlan, O'Donnell, Llewellyn, [Siobhán McSweeney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siobh%C3%A1n_McSweeney "Siobhán McSweeney"), and Jackson all appeared for the special.

In _GBBO_ fashion, there were three challenges to be completed and tasted by judges [Paul Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Hollywood "Paul Hollywood") and [Prue Leith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prue_Leith "Prue Leith"). The first challenge was a [trifle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trifle "Trifle"), then [blinis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blini "Blini") in the technical round, finishing with a showstopper tiered cake that each member had to design in a decades theme. At the end of the competition, Jackson was declared the winner.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-gbbo-72)

_**Derry Girls**_ is a [period](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Historical_drama "Historical drama")[teen sitcom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teen_sitcom "Teen sitcom") set in [Derry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry "Derry"), Northern Ireland, created and written by [Lisa McGee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lisa_McGee "Lisa McGee"), that premiered on 4 January 2018 on UK-based broadcaster [Channel 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Channel_4 "Channel 4")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-BARB-4) and ran for three series. The channel's most successful comedy since _[Father Ted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Father\_Ted "Father Ted")_, the series was inspired by McGee's own experiences growing up in an Irish Catholic family in [Derry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry "Derry"), [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland"), in the 1990s, during the final years of [the Troubles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Troubles "The Troubles").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-5) It stars [Saoirse-Monica Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saoirse-Monica_Jackson "Saoirse-Monica Jackson"), [Louisa Harland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisa_Harland "Louisa Harland"), [Nicola Coughlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Coughlan "Nicola Coughlan"), [Jamie-Lee O'Donnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie-Lee_O'Donnell "Jamie-Lee O'Donnell"), and [Dylan Llewellyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_Llewellyn "Dylan Llewellyn") as five teenagers living in mid-1990s Derry while attending Our Lady Immaculate College, a fictional [girls' Catholic secondary school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_school "Catholic school") based on the real-life [Thornhill College](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thornhill_College "Thornhill College"), where McGee herself studied.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-7) Produced by British production company [Hat Trick Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hat_Trick_Productions "Hat Trick Productions"), _Derry Girls_ was filmed in Northern Ireland, with most scenes shot on location in Derry and some in [Belfast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belfast "Belfast").

Although the plot lines of _Derry Girls_ are fictional, the series frequently references actual events of the Troubles and the [Northern Ireland peace process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland_peace_process "Northern Ireland peace process"), including the 1994 IRA ceasefire announcement, the 1995 visit to Northern Ireland of President [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton") and First Lady [Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton"), and the [Good Friday referendum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Friday_Agreement "Good Friday Agreement") of 1998. Archival footage relating to key political figures such as [Ian Paisley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_Paisley "Ian Paisley"), [Gerry Adams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerry_Adams "Gerry Adams"), [Martin McGuinness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Martin_McGuinness "Martin McGuinness"), [John Hume](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Hume "John Hume") and [Mo Mowlam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mo_Mowlam "Mo Mowlam") is shown via TV and radio broadcasts in family homes. The soundtrack features popular music of the era, by acts including [The Undertones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Undertones "The Undertones"), [Ace of Base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ace_of_Base "Ace of Base"), [Blur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blur_(band) "Blur (band)"), [Cypress Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cypress_Hill "Cypress Hill"), [Salt-N-Pepa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salt-N-Pepa "Salt-N-Pepa"), [Enya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enya "Enya"), [the Corrs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Corrs "The Corrs"), [Boyzone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boyzone "Boyzone"), [Scarlet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarlet_(British_band) "Scarlet (British band)"), [Fatboy Slim](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fatboy_Slim "Fatboy Slim"), [PJ & Duncan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ant_&_Dec_discography "Ant & Dec discography"), and [the Cranberries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Cranberries "The Cranberries").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-8)

The first series, broadcast on Channel 4 in January and February 2018,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-9) became the most-watched series in Northern Ireland since modern records began in 2002. The series was renewed shortly after the pilot episode aired, and the second series was broadcast in March and April 2019. A third and final series set in 1996[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-10) and 1997[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-Special-11) was commissioned for 2020, although filming was delayed due to the [COVID-19 pandemic's impact on television production](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Impact_of_the_COVID-19_pandemic_on_television "Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on television"),[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-13) and premiered in April 2022.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-DG3-15) A final special extended 45-minute episode titled "The Agreement", set in 1998 during the signing of the [Good Friday Agreement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Friday_Agreement "Good Friday Agreement"), aired on 18 May 2022.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-Special-11)

_Derry Girls_ has inspired a mural of its main characters painted on the side of Badgers Bar and Restaurant at 18 Orchard Street, Derry, which has become a popular tourist attraction.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-16)

## Synopsis

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Synopsis")]

The series follows Erin Quinn ([Saoirse-Monica Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saoirse-Monica_Jackson "Saoirse-Monica Jackson")), her cousin Orla ([Louisa Harland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisa_Harland "Louisa Harland")), their friends Clare ([Nicola Coughlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Coughlan "Nicola Coughlan")), Michelle ([Jamie-Lee O'Donnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie-Lee_O'Donnell "Jamie-Lee O'Donnell")), and Michelle's English cousin James ([Dylan Llewellyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_Llewellyn "Dylan Llewellyn")) as they navigate their teenage years during the end of [the Troubles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Troubles "The Troubles") in [Derry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry "Derry"), where they all attend a [Catholic girls' secondary school](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_school "Catholic school"). The friends frequently find themselves in absurd situations amid the political unrest and cultural divides of the times.

## Cast and characters

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Cast and characters")]

### Main

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Main")]

*   [Saoirse-Monica Jackson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saoirse-Monica_Jackson "Saoirse-Monica Jackson") as Erin Quinn. Aged 16 at the start of the series, she is passionate and ambitious, with literary aspirations, but is at times vain, self-centred, or overly concerned with how she is regarded by others.
*   [Louisa Harland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Louisa_Harland "Louisa Harland") as Orla McCool. Aged 15 at the start of the series, she is Erin's detached and eccentric maternal cousin, addicted to sweets. She takes many things literally, misses social cues, and generally is happy to live in her own world.
*   [Nicola Coughlan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nicola_Coughlan "Nicola Coughlan") as Clare Devlin. Intelligent and studious, often the Girls' voice of reason, she is more intimidated than her friends by authority figures. At the end of series one, she [comes out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming_out "Coming out") as a lesbian.
*   [Jamie-Lee O'Donnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jamie-Lee_O'Donnell "Jamie-Lee O'Donnell") as Michelle Mallon. The "wild" one of the group, she often gets her friends into trouble through her keen interest in sex, drugs, and alcohol.
*   [Dylan Llewellyn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dylan_Llewellyn "Dylan Llewellyn") as James Maguire. Michelle's maternal cousin, who has grown up in London but his mother brings him to live in Derry just before the start of the series; she moves back to London without telling him at the end of the first episode. Out of concern for his safety at the local Christian Brothers school, James becomes the first male pupil at Our Lady Immaculate College. Although the girls make fun of James, they care about him and eventually accept him as a Derry Girl. Everyone believes he is gay, despite his protestations.
*   [Tara Lynne O'Neill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tara_Lynne_O'Neill "Tara Lynne O'Neill") as Mary Quinn. Erin and Anna's mother and the matriarch of the Quinn family, she has been married to Gerry for 17 years at the start of the series.
*   [Tommy Tiernan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tommy_Tiernan "Tommy Tiernan") as Gerry Quinn. Mary's husband and Erin and Anna's father, he is from [Navan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navan "Navan") and works as a delivery driver. He has a strained relationship with his father-in-law, and patiently tries to be the voice of reason despite almost constant mockery and dismissal from those around him.
*   [Kathy Kiera Clarke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathy_Kiera_Clarke "Kathy Kiera Clarke") as Sarah McCool. Orla's mother, Erin and Anna's maternal aunt and Mary's younger sister, she is sweet but dim-witted, heavily focused on her own and other people's appearances. She is an inattentive mother and takes little responsibility for raising Orla, but is still very affectionate towards her.
*   [Ian McElhinney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ian_McElhinney "Ian McElhinney") as Joe McCool. Mary and Sarah's father, and Erin, Anna and Orla's grandfather, he moved in with the Quinns after his wife died ten years before the start of the series. Joe shows nothing but contempt for Gerry, constantly criticising him and encouraging Mary to leave him, and is fiercely protective of his daughters and granddaughters.
*   [Siobhán McSweeney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siobh%C3%A1n_McSweeney "Siobhán McSweeney") as Sister George Michael, a [Catholic nun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_nun "Catholic nun"). The headmistress of Our Lady Immaculate College, she rules the school with an iron fist. Acid-tongued and unflappable, she views being a nun as a job rather than a calling, treating priests with indifference or even contempt.
*   [Leah O'Rourke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leah_O'Rourke "Leah O'Rourke") as Jenny Joyce, a [prefect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/School_prefect "School prefect") and sycophant despised by the Girls. She is from a wealthy family and lives in a large house with eight bedrooms, in which she often hosts lavish parties. Her mother Janette used to be friends with Mary, Sarah, Geraldine (Clare's mum) and Deirdre (Michelle's mum) when they were teenagers but since distanced herself after marrying a surgeon.

### Recurring

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Recurring")]

*   Ava Grace McAleese and Mya Rose McAleese as Anna Quinn, Erin's toddler sister. She is often seen in the arms of Granda Joe.
*   Beccy Henderson as Aisling, Jenny's best friend and sidekick. As they often duet together, it is made clear that Jenny is tone-deaf whilst Aisling is musically talented.
*   [Claire Rafferty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claire_Rafferty_(actress) "Claire Rafferty (actress)") as Miss Mooney, Sister Michael's deputy.
*   [Amelia Crowley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amelia_Crowley "Amelia Crowley") as Deirdre Mallon, Michelle's mother and James' maternal aunt, a nurse.
*   [Kevin McAleer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_McAleer "Kevin McAleer") as Colm McCool, Joe's brother, Erin, Orla and Anna's great-uncle and Mary and Sarah's uncle, known for telling pointless stories in a slow, ponderous style, with numerous digressions, though if they are listened to properly they are actually quite entertaining. He is always oblivious to everyone's open boredom during his stories and seems not to notice their attempts to make him stop. His family avoids him whenever possible.
*   Paul Mallon as Dennis, the aggressive proprietor of the corner shop the Girls frequent. His merchandise is often cheap and irregular, such as purple US flags with only 30 stars, for which he overcharges.
*   [Philippa Dunne](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Philippa_Dunne "Philippa Dunne") as Geraldine Devlin, Clare's mother. She seems to be under the belief her daughter is a delinquent, though they are incredibly similar in their anxious temperaments. As with everyone else in the show, she accepts and supports her daughter's sexuality.
*   [Peter Campion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Campion_(actor) "Peter Campion (actor)") as Father Peter Conway, a young priest on whom most of the Girls initially have a crush. In the first series, he leaves the priesthood to begin a relationship with a hairdresser, before returning as a priest again in later series. Sister Michael openly despises him and dreads his visits.
*   Jamie Beamish as Ciaran, Sarah's eager-to-please love interest, who works at a photography chain store.
*   Robert Calvert as Jim, the Quinns' neighbour across the road. Joe relies on Jim to lend him various things such as a tent and a tranquilliser gun, and the two share occasional schemes together.
*   Maria Laird as Tina O'Connell, a confident first-year student, who is able to intimidate older classmates through her sister, "Big Mandy", who also attends the school.
*   [Ardal O'Hanlon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ardal_O'Hanlon "Ardal O'Hanlon") as Eamonn, Mary and Sarah's maternal first cousin, who moves in with the Quinns in the final episode of the series after his roof collapses.
*   [Liam Neeson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liam_Neeson "Liam Neeson") as Chief Constable Byers. When the Girls are arrested for stealing computers from the school, he interviews them and is forced to listen to Uncle Colm when they call him for support.
*   [David Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Ireland_(playwright) "David Ireland (playwright)") as Sean Devlin, Clare's father. In the penultimate episode of the series, he suffers an [aneurysm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aneurysm "Aneurysm") and dies, leading Clare and her mother to move away from Derry.
*   Julia Dearden as Maureen Malarkey, an elderly neighbour of the Quinns. She and Joe share a bitter [bingo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bingo_(British_version) "Bingo (British version)") rivalry.
*   [Anthony Boyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Boyle "Anthony Boyle") as David Donnelly, a boy on whom Erin has a crush in the first series.

### Guest appearances

Erin's crush David Donnelly invites her to his band's gig that evening. Michelle introduces her English cousin James to Erin, Clare, and Orla. A fight on the school bus lands the group in detention. The almost 98-year-old Sister Declan confiscates Michelle's lipstick and Erin's diary while supervising them, but then suddenly dies. Sister Michael enters to find Michelle retrieving her lipstick, Erin climbing out a window in an effort to get to David's gig, Clare (on a 24-hour fast to raise money for an African charity) devouring the remains of Sister Declan's sandwich, and James (barred from the female-only toilets) urinating into a bin. The friends' parents are summoned, and James discovers that his mother has gone back to London without him. Upon getting suspended, Orla once again reads aloud Erin's diary, causing the latter to aggressively retrieve it while threatening Orla. |

At the chip shop, they see a noticeboard advertising part-time jobs, and decide to earn the money to fund their trip. Joe's brother Colm, notorious for his monotonous stories, visits Erin's family to recount how two IRA terrorists tied him to his radiator by his shoelaces and stole his van to transport weapons across the [border](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republic_of_Ireland-United_Kingdom_border "Republic of Ireland-United Kingdom border"). Sarah and Colm are later interviewed by [UTV](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTV_(TV_channel) "UTV (TV channel)"). Michelle steals the chip shop noticeboard so the friends will be the only job applicants. The intimidating owner Fionnula discovers the theft after Clare tells her mother. To make amends, the friends clean her shop while she attends a yoga class, but Michelle accidentally sets fire to the flat above the shop with [flaming shots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flaming_drink "Flaming drink"). The teens call Mary and Sarah, who tie them by their shoelaces to the radiators, intending to pretend that IRA terrorists tried to steal Fionnula's van. Michelle plays along, believing the friends will not have to sit their exam if they are witnesses to a miracle. A handsome young priest, Father Peter, investigates. He suggests that Toto was resurrected to lead Erin to the church, which appears to be confirmed when Toto's grave in the [back garden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back_garden "Back garden") is discovered to be empty. Overhearing her mother on the phone, Erin finds out that Mary faked Toto's death and gave the dog to their elderly neighbour. The friends maintain the hoax until Peter reveals to Erin that he was close to abandoning the priesthood to pursue a relationship. Believing he is attracted to her, Erin tells him the truth. On the front page of the _[Derry Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry\_Journal "Derry Journal")_, the friends are branded liars who pranked the [Catholic Church](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church") and have to take their exam after all. |

Katya explains she was collecting money from the other Ukrainians to buy Jenny a thank-you gift. Michelle discovers 'Artem' is actually Clive, a [Protestant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulster_Protestants "Ulster Protestants") from East [Belfast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belfast "Belfast") who took a wrong turn leaving [Aldergrove Airport](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldergrove_Airport "Aldergrove Airport"); terrified of the [Catholics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irish_Catholics "Irish Catholics"), he pretended to be one of the Ukrainians. The group departs in two cars, with Joe insisting on navigating, only to lead the group into the middle of a hostile Orange parade. Sarah tells Michelle's [fortune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortune-telling "Fortune-telling"), predicting she will soon meet her future husband. After the group finally leaves Derry and drives toward the border, they discover an [Irish Republican Army](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Provisional_Irish_Republican_Army "Provisional Irish Republican Army") (IRA) terrorist hiding in their [boot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trunk_(car) "Trunk (car)"). Using the false name Emmett, he tells them he urgently needs to cross the border. Gerry and Joe argue over whether to risk arrest by transporting Emmett, while Michelle believes Emmett to be her future husband. As Gerry and Joe continue to disagree, Emmett flees the restaurant where they stopped for lunch, steals their tent—borrowed from their neighbour Jim—and departs in the boot of another car as the group watches. |

Needing a lead story, she finds an anonymous entry by a lesbian pupil in the school's "Searching for Myself" writing contest. She prints it under the headline "The Secret Life of a Lesbian!" Sister Michael assumes the friends are wearing pink shirts to support [gay rights](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LGBT_rights_by_country_or_territory "LGBT rights by country or territory"), and bans the issue. The friends distribute it regardless, creating a sensation within the school. Clare [comes out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coming_out "Coming out") to Erin, confiding that she wrote the story, but Erin reacts negatively and the two fall out. At the school talent show, Orla performs a [step aerobics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Step_aerobics "Step aerobics") routine, eliciting ridicule. Coming to her defence, Erin, Clare, Michelle, and James join her onstage, ending Erin and Clare's feud. As the friends dance joyfully at school, Mary, Gerry, Sarah, and Joe watch sombrely at home as news reports of a fatal bombing filter through. |

## Production

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Production")]

Filming took place in [Northern Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Northern_Ireland "Northern Ireland"), with most scenes shot in [Derry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry "Derry") and [Belfast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Belfast "Belfast").[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-21) The scenes onboard the train in S3 E3 took place at the [Downpatrick and County Down Railway](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downpatrick_and_County_Down_Railway "Downpatrick and County Down Railway") in [Downpatrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Downpatrick "Downpatrick"),[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-22) with the end of the episode shot at the then-recently-closed [Barry's Amusements](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barry's_Amusements "Barry's Amusements") in [Portrush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portrush "Portrush").[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-23) The first series was filmed from May to July 2017 and released in January and February 2018.

The show was renewed for a second series shortly after the airing of the pilot episode of the first series. Production of the second series began on 8 October 2018.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-25) The second series began airing on 5 March 2019.[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-S2-17) On 9 April 2019, immediately after the second series finale, it was confirmed by Channel 4 that _Derry Girls_ would return for a third series.[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-27) Production of the third series was due to commence in the spring of 2020, but was suspended following the announcement of the [COVID-19 lockdown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_lockdowns "COVID-19 lockdowns").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-28) On 21 July 2021, Nicola Coughlan confirmed that filming for the third series was set to commence in late 2021, with a premiere in early 2022.[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-29) On 23 September 2021, series creator and writer Lisa McGee confirmed Derry Girls would end with its third series, stating "it was always the plan to say goodbye after three series."[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-30) On 21 December 2021, McGee and Coughlan announced on social media that filming of the final series had completed.[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-radiotimes-31)

## Broadcast

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Broadcast")]

The first series premiered on Channel 4 in the United Kingdom on Thursday nights at 10:00 pm, while the second series was moved to Tuesday nights at 9:15 pm, with the exception of the sixth episode, which was aired at 9:00 pm. The entire series is available to stream in the UK on [All 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/All_4 "All 4").

The series was picked up by [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") internationally, with series 1 being released on 21 December 2018.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-32) Series 2 was released on 2 August 2019.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-33) The international version of the first series is now available to stream on Netflix in the UK and Ireland. The second series was added on 9 July 2020; however, it was temporarily removed from the service, as it was mistakenly released a year early.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-34) The third and final series was released on 7 October 2022.[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-35)

## Reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=12 "Edit section: Reception")]

_Derry Girls_ became Channel 4's most successful comedy since _[Father Ted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Father\_Ted "Father Ted")_.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-McClements-37) On [Rotten Tomatoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotten_Tomatoes "Rotten Tomatoes"), the first series holds an approval rating of 100% based on reviews from 24 critics with an average rating of 7.9/10. The website's critics consensus states: "A perfectly curated cast and raw writing drive _Derry Girls_'s dark humor as creator Lisa McGee makes frenetic light of teen life in 1990s Northern Ireland".[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-38)

The second series has an approval rating of 97%, based on reviews from 33 critics with an average rating of 8.3/10. The website's critics consensus states: "The sophomore season of _Derry Girls_ doesn't lose any of its irreverent charms thanks to its predictably unpredictable romps and canny characterizations".[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-39)

The third series holds an approval rating of 100%, based on reviews from 21 critics with an average rating of 8.9/10. The website's critics consensus states: "Parting is such sweet sorrow, but _Derry Girls_' final season promises to milk as many laughs as it can before viewers say a fond farewell to this lovable band of miscreants."[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-40) On [Metacritic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacritic "Metacritic"), which uses a weighted average, it received a score of 86 out of 100 based on five critic reviews.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-41)

[![Image 6](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/07/Derry_Girls_Mural_-_geograph.org.uk_-_7105686.jpg/250px-Derry_Girls_Mural_-_geograph.org.uk_-_7105686.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Derry_Girls_Mural_-_geograph.org.uk_-_7105686.jpg)

Derry Girls Mural in Derry, Northern Ireland

_Derry Girls_ was the most watched series in Northern Ireland since modern records began in 2002, with an average audience of 519,000 and a 64.2 per cent share of the audience.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-42)[Una Mullally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Una_Mullally "Una Mullally") of _[The Irish Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Irish\_Times "The Irish Times")_ praised the series: "The writing in _Derry Girls_ is sublime, the performances perfect, the casting is brilliant."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-43) On 11 January 2018, after the first episode had aired, the programme was renewed for a second series.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-ratings-44) Each episode was watched by over two million people.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-BARB-4) At the conclusion of the first series, Barbara Ellen of _[The Guardian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Guardian "The Guardian")_ wrote that _Derry Girls_ evoked such programmes as _[The Inbetweeners](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Inbetweeners "The Inbetweeners")_, _[Father Ted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Father\_Ted "Father Ted")_ and _[Bad Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bad\_Education\_(TV\_series) "Bad Education (TV series)")_.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-45)

### Public reception

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=13 "Edit section: Public reception")]

As there are slight political undertones to the show, responses have highlighted the comedic nature as keeping the material lighthearted enough to enjoy. Certain writers from various online articles have noted that their own Northern Irish family appreciated the way the show gave an honest portrayal of how life was for teens in the Troubles, and how much was endured by families during that time.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-N._Jones_2019-46) The way it portrayed the events and circumstances with a sense of normality echoed the real lives of both Protestants and Catholics in that area.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-N._Jones_2019-46)

Lisa McGee based events in the programme on her own life, such as writing a letter to the [Clintons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clinton_family "Clinton family")' daughter, Chelsea.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-47) Adding real stories such as this to the episodes grounded the show in a way that allowed viewers to connect with the teenage attitudes of the characters, and served as a stark contrast to the events around them. The juxtaposition of the Troubles violence and teenage life resonated with many viewers.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-48) At 18 Orchard Street in Derry,[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-49) a mural of the main cast of characters can be seen on the side of Badger's Bar.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-McClements-37)

### _Great British Bake Off_ New Year's episode

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Derry_Girls&action=edit&section=20 "Edit section: Great British Bake Off New Year's episode")]

For the 2020 New Year holiday, the cast competed on a special episode of _[The Great British Bake Off](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The\_Great\_British\_Bake\_Off "The Great British Bake Off")_. Cast members Coughlan, O'Donnell, Llewellyn, [Siobhán McSweeney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siobh%C3%A1n_McSweeney "Siobhán McSweeney"), and Jackson all appeared for the special.

In _GBBO_ fashion, there were three challenges to be completed and tasted by judges [Paul Hollywood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Hollywood "Paul Hollywood") and [Prue Leith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prue_Leith "Prue Leith"). The first challenge was a [trifle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trifle "Trifle"), then [blinis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blini "Blini") in the technical round, finishing with a showstopper tiered cake that each member had to design in a decades theme. At the end of the competition, Jackson was declared the winner.[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Derry_Girls#cite_note-gbbo-72)
